says: next/: RepositoriesGit.test.ts's L10 ("success, refusal and interruption release every acquired Git child and temporary directory") runs in the `next` project, which pull requests and the merge queue run, and on every third tape cell it starts a real Node child (`ChildProcess.make(process.execPath, ["-e", "setInterval(() => {}, 1000)"])`), a spawned process, which 0536 keeps off the merge line. Its git commands do run on memory git; only this stand-in child is real.
proof: GitLaws.test-support.ts builds memory git over the platform's spawner, which runs every command that is not git. On 2026-11-14 a scratch script in the worktree (deleted after) provided `GitLaws.gits`' memory services and ran `process.execPath -e "console.log(process.pid)"` through `ChildProcessSpawner.string`: it printed `layers: memory this pid: 54233 child pid: 54953`, a second real process. The lint rule `fabrika/integration-test-name` does not fire, since it reads `node:child_process` calls only, not Effect's `ChildProcess.make`.
cost: Every pull request that reaches RepositoriesGit.test.ts starts dozens of real Node processes (100 runs of tapes of 1 to 4 cells, a child for every cell whose number is 2 mod 3), against 0536's binding constraint, and the integration-name rule cannot see it. Moving L10 to an `*.integration.test.ts` file would take the law off the merge line; an in-memory child handle that never ends would keep it there.
